correctness.rationale: Equal three-round firing counts follow from the connected Laplacian kernel. Explicit degree-two phase enumeration leaves exactly three peripheral pattern pairs; hub degree \(2k\) threshold yields \(0\le r\le k-a-1\), directly producing polynomial coefficients. Bounded chip complementation produces the reflected band and preserves primitive period. Binomial size bias proves the two-uniform limit. A direct finite state checker tested all 1,099,840 bounded configurations for \(1\le k\le4\), and a separate firing-word inequality checker reproduced the exact coefficients for \(1\le k\le12\); both scripts and outputs are embedded.

Known general chip-firing period and firing-pattern theorems, one-resonant-cycle results, and other graph-family mass polynomials do not cover these exact coefficients; the 2024 forbidden middle-stair theorem supplies only exclusions, not the attained sharp endpoints. value.rationale: The exact infinite-family mass polynomial classifies all immediate primitive-three recurrent states on an arbitrarily large multi-resonant triangular cactus with one articulation point. Its support meets both sharp limits of the known universal period-three excluded middle interval, and a nontrivial two-uniform normalized mass law emerges. This is neither a textbook reduction of the universal theorem nor a handful of finite examples.
